<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #20679

Problem Summary:
Currently all values must be defined in the partitioning definitions, which is not very user friendly. By allowing a DEFAULT partition, as a catch-all partition, one only need to define the most occurring values and have the DEFAULT partition catch the rest.

### What is changed and how it works?
For insert/update, the pruning is simple, if no match on defined values and there exists a default partition, put the new value there.

For select pruning, we will add the default partition if the existing values are not matched or there are multiple partitioning columns (due to the combination check needs a further refactoring) or if there is a range.

Since this is a compatibility breaker for MySQL (but not completely for MariaDB), I also added `tidb_enable_default_list_partition` variable that is default OFF.

One difference from the syntax of MariaDB and Oracle is that it allows both `(DEFAULT)` and `(<list of values>)` in a partition definition, which if used, it is not supported by MariaDB (I'm OK to remove this enhancement, since functionally it does not make sense, but it may be better usability to have the known values there, instead of like in a comment).

Documentation

#### Manual testing
```bash
make
tiup playground nightly --db.binpath ~/repos/tidb/bin/tidb-server
```
```mysql
drop table if exists t;
set tidb_enable_default_list_partition=1;
create table t
(a bigint unsigned,
 b bigint unsigned,
 c varchar(768),
 primary key (a,b),
 key (c))
partition by list(b)
(partition p1 values in (0,1,4,5,6,7,9),
 partition p2 values in (11,13,12,15,16,17,18),
 partition p3 values in (22,21,default,66,220));
insert into t values (1,1,"Z"),(2,2,"y"),(3,3,"q"),(4,4,"R"),(5,5,"M");
insert into t values (15,15,"W"),(17,17,"N"),(220,220,"T"),(66,66,"o"),(10,10,"z");
insert into t values (6,6,"p"),(7,7,"B"),(8,8,"a"),(9,9,"i"),(11,11,"n");
analyze table t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,0),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t; 
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,1),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,2),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,3),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,4),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,5),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,6),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,7),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,8),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,9),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,10),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,11),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,12),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,13),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,14),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,15),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,16),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,17),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,18),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t order by a,b limit 1600000;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,19),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t order by a,b limit 1600000;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,20),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t order by a,b limit 1600000;
insert into t select `a`+pow(2,21),b,concat(`a`,`c`) from t order by a,b limit 1600000;
select count(*), sum(a), sum(b) from t;
# +----------+---------------+----------+
# | count(*) | sum(a)        | sum(b)   |
# +----------+---------------+----------+
# | 10332160 | 7148444658184 | 264327144 |
# +----------+---------------+----------+
```
```bash
 ./bin/br restore full --storage 'local:///backup/defaultlist'
```
Then drop the table, or start a new cluster
```mysql
drop table t;
```
And Restore
```bash
./bin/br restore full --storage 'local:///backup/defaultlist'
```
And check the table contains the same
```mysql
select count(*), sum(a), sum(b) from t;
# +----------+---------------+----------+
# | count(*) | sum(a)        | sum(b)   |
# +----------+---------------+----------+
# | 10332160 | 7148444658184 | 264327144 |
# +----------+---------------+----------+
```
### Release note

<!-- compatibility change, improvement, bugfix, and new feature need a release note -->

Please refer to [Release Notes Language Style Guide](https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/release-notes-style-guide.html) to write a quality release note.

```release-note
Adding support for a default partition in LIST [COLUMNS] partitioning.
```

issue_context.title: Support default partition for list (columns) partition table
issue_context.body:
## Feature Request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:**

N/A

**Describe the feature you'd like:**

The default partition of list partition table is from [ORACLE](https://docs.oracle.com/database/121/VLDBG/GUID-8928C3B0-2F83-4213-B765-EFBBF0372F64.htm), MYSQL doesn't support this, but it is a very useful feature.

Here is an example, I want to create a list partition table, the list partition depends on the year.

```sql
create table t (a date) partition by list (year(a)) (
    partition p0 values in (2020));
```

But I execute the following SQL will fail:

```sql
> insert into t values ('2019-10-27 17:36:10');
(1526, 'Table has no partition for value 2019')
```  

I know the upper behavior is expected, So I want to add a default partition to store the data that doesn't match the other partitions. Such as:

```sql
create table t (a date) partition by list (year(a)) (
    partition p0 values in (2020), 
    partition p1 values in (default));
```

Then the following SQL will be successfully inserted into the default partition.

```sql
insert into t values ('2019-10-27 17:36:10'),('2021-10-27 17:36:10'),('2000-10-27 17:36:10');
```
```
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```
**Another feature-request is**, should we support the ORACLE list partition syntax? Some customers are using ORACLE syntax to test the list partition.


**Describe alternatives you've considered:**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->

The upper features aren't hard to implement, I already implemented this here: https://github.com/bb7133/tidb/pull/33


**Teachability, Documentation, Adoption, Migration Strategy:**
<!-- If you can, explain some scenarios how users might use this, situations it would be helpful in. Any API designs, mockups, or diagrams are also helpful. -->

N/A
comments:
I noticed that there is a worklog in MySQL which discusses to support the `default` list partition: [WL#5781: DEFAULT/catch-all partition for LIST partitioning](https://dev.mysql.com/worklog/task/?id=5781), the feature request in MySQL is [Bug #50566](https://bugs.mysql.com/bug.php?id=50566).

The Syntax is like Oracle:


```sql
CREATE TABLE t (a INT, b TEXT)
PARTITION BY LIST (a)
(PARTITION p0 VALUES IN (1,5,6,7),
 PARTITION p1 VALUES IN (3,4,9),
 PARTITION pDefault VALUES IN (DEFAULT));
```

Please note:

> When using a DEFAULT partition, it will not longer be possible to ADD a partition, but one must instead REORGANIZE the DEFAULT partition, just like MAXVALUE partition in RANGE partitioning.

> Another feature-request is, should we support the ORACLE list partition syntax? Some customers are using ORACLE syntax to test the list partition.

@crazycs520 I think it's better to keep the MySQL syntax since we are claimed to be MySQL compatible. BTW, it's better to discuss only one feature request at one issue.

review_comments:
From https://dev.mysql.com/worklog/task/?id=5781:

> When using a DEFAULT partition, it will not longer be possible to ADD a partition, but one must instead REORGANIZE the DEFAULT partition, just like MAXVALUE partition in RANGE partitioning.

Now we allow `ADD PARTITION` without reorganizing the data, is it expected?
I added a check for that `checkAddListPartitions`.
